entertainment.title: Sharon Osbourne Visits Late Husband Ozzy’s Grave Every Day: ‘You Never Get Over It’
entertainment.summary: The metal icon's wife/manager said all the flowers left behind in Birmingham have been composed for the family garden, where Ozzy is buried.
entertainment.body:
It’s been more than a year since Ozzy Osbourne shuffled off this mortal coil. But according to the late heavy metal icon’s wife/manager, Sharon Osbourne, she still visits the Blizzard of Oz every day. Explore Ozzy Osbourne Sharon Osbourne See latest videos, charts and news

“You’ve lost the love of your life, so you don’t just wake up and go, ‘I’m fine now. I’m cured.’ You never get over it. But you learn to live with it, and that’s what I’m trying to do. So you either sit in a room and don’t come out, or you accept it, befriend it, and that’s it,” Sharon Osbourne told the BBC . Related Lana Del Rey Helps Stranger 'Trying to Stay Out of an Abusive Relationship' While Listening to Tate McRae Cedella Marley Still Believes in the 'Reggae Girlz': 'I Wanted the Music to Reflect the Journey of These Women' Weezer & Wednesday Top Alternative Airplay With 'We Might as Well Be Strangers'

Sharon said the family collected all the cards and messages left at public memorials in Ozzy’s hometown of Birmingham, England, as well as the floral tributes left behind by the thousands who attended the Rock & Roll Hall of Famer’s public funeral procession in his hometown on July 30, 2025 following his death on July 22 at age 76. The items have been sorted and photographed, while the flowers were composted into the family garden at their 250-acre private estate, Welders House, in Buckinghamshire.

“There was no way I could put Ozzy in a public graveyard,” said Sharon. “I’ve seen what happens to other people in the public eye. There’s no peace because people want to come and they want to pay their respects. That’s an ongoing thing, and I wanted Ozzy to rest and just be.”

Asked how often she visit’s Ozzy’s grave, Sharon said, “of course, every day. I can see him from my window.” Sharon said she also talks to her late husband of half a century “regularly,” though she declined to reveal what they discuss.

Sharon also described the elation Ozzy felt when, against his doctor’s wishes, he was able to play one last triumphal show, the all-star Back to the Beginning blow-out , at his beloved Villa park football pitch in his hometown of Birmingham. Though back problems and Parkinson’s disease symptoms had made it impossible for Ozzy to tour in his later years, Sharon said after the one-off swan song gig the Prince of Darkness was riding high.

“He was just so, so happy,” she said of his mood after the 11-hour show that featured him performing solo and with Black Sabbath, as well as tributes from Metallica, Slayer, Guns ‘N Roses, Pantera, Tool and many more. “He was online going through the reviews and saying, ‘There’s something terribly wrong,’ and I’m like, ‘why?’,” she remembered. “He goes, ‘I didn’t get slagged by anybody. entertainment.title: Ava DuVernay Defends Using AI in New Doc ’14th’
entertainment.summary: The director wants audiences to "make their decisions about how they feel" about the technology, which is used to bring to life some archival photos in the film.
entertainment.body:
As Ava DuVernay continues to hit the festival circuit for her new documentary 14th , the director is opening up about her decision to use AI on elements of the film.

The doc is a deep dive on the Constitution’s 14th Amendment and the fight over birthright citizenship, featuring archival photographs that are brought to life with the help of AI. This has sparked some criticism online, which DuVernay addressed to The Hollywood Reporter as the doc screened at AFI Fest on Sunday.

“The tools that the artists used to do the parallax and the animation in the films have that technology in it, as does Pro Tools with sound, as does Avid with editorial, as does Resolve with color,” she said of industry post-production tools. “I think we’ve come to a place in filmmaking where we have to be really sober about the ways in which that technology is [used] across so much of the workflow.” Related Stories Business Anthropic Warns in IPO Filing That Unfavorable Media Coverage of AI Could "Adversely Affect" Its Business Music Anthropic Sued for Using Elvis Presley Music to Train AI Models

She continued of the AI, “We didn’t use it to fabricate a person or make an avatar of a person or approximate someone’s voice that said something they didn’t say. We actually animated some photos that are in the public domain, and from what we’ve been hearing from people it does bring people closer to that time in history, which was our goal. So people have to see it and check it out for themselves and make their decisions about how they feel.”

14th comes a decade after DuVernay’s Oscar-nominated doc 13th , exploring the U.S. prison system and racial inequality in the light of the 13th Amendment. However, she doesn’t see the new film as a direct follow-up, and started considering a return to the Constitution after “hearing the current president talking about his desire to dismantle birthright citizenship while he was a candidate; he said he would do it in his first week in office. He actually did it in his first day in office, he attacked birthright citizenship.”

“I don’t know much about the 14th Amendment at that point but I know birthright citizenship is in it. So we start thinking about the possibility of making this film at that point,” the filmmaker said, and “once we saw all of the tentacles of the current administration attacking this amendment, we knew that there was more there. So we investigated it and that’s what the film became.”

Starting Monday, Instagram will be launching a test of horizontal videos of up to 90 minutes with select creators in the U.S. The product, called Features, is aimed at podcasters, comedians and other long-form creators, with the ability to refer viewers to the full video from the short-form reels on the platform, which are typically around three minutes or less.

“What you’re now going to be able to do is, you see a clip of a podcast that you love, you can just click and continue watching or watch the full video, and you’ll be able to dive in and see the whole thing because creators are going to be able to link these Reels to their overall feature,” said Tessa Lyons, vice president of product at Instagram.

Instagram has already been testing the feature with creators in Brazil and has a plan of expanding to tens of thousands of creators in the U.S. The videos will also be recommended to users on Instagram’s Explore page and in other areas. Early creators involved in the test include podcast host and Skims co-founder Emma Grede, beauty and fashion creator Monet McMichael, Preston Rakovsky, who interviews New Yorkers about love and relationships and football content creator Donald De La Haye.

This comes as Netflix, Disney and more have been adding podcasts and videos from creators to their platforms, in an effort to capture more consumer viewing hours, and compete with entertainment behemoth YouTube. One challenge for Instagram and others, in the battle against YouTube, has been competing against the platform’s lucrative revenue sharing deals, with YouTube offering qualified creators offered 55 percent of ad revenue and helping generate brand deals.

Lyons said Instagram is currently working on “a few different deals” with the early creators for Features, but there’s currently no exclusivity around putting the videos on Instagram (unlike Netflix’s deals for podcasts). Additionally, existing ad deals will carry over into the videos, but Instagram will also work with creators without existing placements to find deals.

“For established creators who already have those relationships, they can bring that content with those placements and that branded content. And we also think that there’s a big opportunity for us to help creators who don’t yet have that infrastructure and that business behind them,” Lyons said.

entertainment.title: From CMA New Artist Award Nominees to the Country Music Hall of Fame: 14 Artists Who Made the Journey
entertainment.summary: It's the journey every new artist in country music dreams of making.
entertainment.body:
As Avery Anna , Carter Faith , Emily Ann Roberts , Tucker Wetmore and Stephen Wilson Jr. settle into their seats at Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena on Nov. 18 for this year’s CMA Awards, anxiously awaiting to hear which of them will take home the award for new artist of the year, they should keep in mind that this is just the start of their journey. If they’re lucky, their careers will continue for decades, and if they’re really lucky, they’ll one day be enshrined in the Country Music Hall of Fame.

The CMA introduced the Horizon Award – the award’s original name — in 1981; it was renamed new artist of the year in 2008. Since then, 14 artists who were nominated in that category have gone on to be inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame. The most recent case is Tim McGraw , who was nominated for the Horizon Award in 1994 and was elected to the Country Music Hall of Fame this year.

You may have noticed that I said McGraw was nominated for the Horizon Award. He didn’t win. He’s not alone in that. Nine of the 14 artists who were nominated for the Horizon Award and went on to be inducted into the Hall of Fame didn’t win the newcomer award. Patty Loveless was nominated twice and lost both times – to Ricky Van Shelton in 1988 and to Clint Black in 1989. (Neither of those men has yet been inducted into the Country Music HOF, though they may be in the future.)

Moral of the story: If you’re nominated for a new artist award and don’t win, keep going. There are many chapters ahead of you.

Garth Brooks was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame just 22 years after he was nominated for (and won) the Horizon Award – the fastest climb of any artist. Other artists who made this climb quickly are George Strait (23 years), Kenny Chesney (26 years) and Alan Jackson and Brooks & Dunn (27 years each).

Here’s a complete list of the 14 artists who were nominated for the CMA’s Horizon Award and went on to be inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame. We show the year they were nominated for (and in some cases, won) the award; the year they were inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame, their number of CMA Awards to date; their number of No. 1 hits on Billboard ’s Hot Country Songs chart to date; and their number of No. 1 albums on Billboard ’s Top Country Albums chart to date.

We’ll update this list in years to come as more Horizon Award, and eventually new artist of the year nominees/winners, are inducted into the Hall.

entertainment.title: ‘Bluey’ Soundtrack Gets the Box Set Treatment With New Collectible Vinyl Release
entertainment.summary: The Amazon-exclusive set includes all four of the 'Bluey' albums pressed on colored vinyl for the first time.
entertainment.body:

Fans of the hit animated children’s series Bluey now have a whole new way to experience the show with The Bluey Album Box Set , which brings the music of the show to vinyl for the very first time.

The Amazon-exclusive set includes all four of the Bluey soundtrack albums: The Album, Dance Mode!, Rug Island and Up Here . Written and arranged by lead composer Joff Bush, the songs include the Bluey theme song, along with memorable tunes like “Keepy Uppy,” “Sleepytime” and “Cat Squad.”

The box set includes four LPs pressed on colored vinyl, with accompanying full color album sleeves and a pull-out panoramic poster. Everything is stored inside a slipcover box. There are more than 60 songs in total collected in this set.

The Album is pressed on a white and blue vinyl disc inspired by the show logo, while Dance Mode! is pressed on pink and orange vinyl, inspired by Bluey’s favorite toy, Chattermax. Rug Island — named after a season two episode where the characters use their imagination to create an island from a rug, throw cushions and colored pens — comes on a green and orange LP. Up Here is pressed on a “blue space”-inspired vinyl. This is an Amazon-exclusive release, meaning the retailer is the only place to find this Bluey music set online. You can also shop official Bluey merch on Amazon here .

All of Bluey’s soundtrack albums have hit the Billboard Kids Album Chart, along with the Billboard Soundtrack Chart. The first release, The Album , debuted at number one on the ARIA Albums Chart in Australia in February 2021, becoming the first children’s album to reach the top of the charts Down Under.

The music box set is a great gift idea for Bluey fans and vinyl collectors alike, and comes on the heels of a host of Bluey holiday releases, including an official advent calendar .

entertainment.title: Mary J. Blige Partners With Primary Wave on Her Iconic Music Catalog
entertainment.summary: The deal includes such hits as "Family Affair," "My Life," "Mary Jane (All Night Long)," "You Bring Me Joy" and "Be Happy."
entertainment.body:
Primary Wave Music has partnered with Mary J. Blige on her catalog compositions and recordings, the company announced Monday (Oct. 26). Through the deal, the publisher will work alongside the iconic singer-songwriter and her team on potential new music marketing, branding, digital and synch opportunities.

According to a press release, Blige has sold more than 50 million records globally. Her catalog includes 15 studio albums, two live albums and 83 singles. She has received nine Grammys from 37 nominations, 12 Billboard Music Awards and has been nominated for two Oscars, among other accolades. She was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2024.

Long dubbed the Queen of Hip-Hop Soul, Blige has racked up six Billboard Hot 100 top 10 hits, including one No. 1, 2001’s “Family Affair.” She’s also charted 14 top 10 albums on the Billboard 200, including four No. 1s: 1997’s Share My World , 2003’s Love & Life , 2006’s The Breakthrough and 2008’s Growing Pains . She burst onto the scene with her 1992 debut album What’s the 411? , which has been certified four-times platinum by the RIAA.

The Primary Wave deal includes such hits as “Family Affair,” “My Life,” “Mary Jane (All Night Long),” “You Bring Me Joy,” “Be Happy,” “Be Without You” and “I Can Love You.”

Earlier this year, Blige announced her Las Vegas residency, Mary J. Blige: My Life, My Story The Las Vegas Residency, at Dolby Live at Park MGM. Kicking off in May, the residency has been extended through February 2027.

In addition to music, Blige has starred in films including Mudbound , for which she received two Oscar nominations: best supporting actress and best original song for the track “Mighty River.” She also recently wrapped an acting stint on the Starz series Power Book II: Ghost .

“From the moment I heard ‘You Remind Me’ on NY’s KISS-FM, I became a Day 1 Mary J Blige fan,” said Natalia Nastaskin , Primary Wave’s chief content officer, in a statement. “For over 30 years, she has gifted the world with hit after undeniable hit and in the process has created the soundtrack of our lives. To partner with the Queen herself on her extraordinary catalog and her everlasting legacy is an honor for me and for our entire Primary Wave team.”
